summary: Francis Brinkley, who studied at Royal School Dungannon, worked in Japanology and other fields. He held a post at the University of Tokyo from circa 1878 to 1886.

Francis Buchanan-Hamilton studied at the University of Edinburgh under John Hope (M.D. ~1780-1783). Active in history, archaeology, and other fields, he served in the Bengal Medical Service, directed the Indian Botanic Garden (1814-1815), and became Keeper at Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh (1815-1829).

Francis Gladwin was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. A founding member of The Asiatic Society (~1784-1812), which he founded, he was appointed the first Professor of Persian at Fort William College in 1801.

Francis Harold Cook, who completed his doctoral requirements at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1965-1970), worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He was Professor at UC Riverside (~1970-1989) and later chaired the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (1999).
Francis John Monahan, a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology, studied at Balliol College, Oxford in 1883. He served as a civil servant in the Indian Civil Service from 1885.

Francis Louis Noël Goré studied at the Séminaire des Missions Étrangères de Paris (~1903-1905) and College General (~1905-1907). Active in Tibetology and religious studies, he served as vicaire apostolique and procureur at Tsechung in the Tibet Mission (1931-1952).

Francis N. J. works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned a Master's in Ancient History at the University of Calicut and completed doctoral studies under the supervision of M. R. Raghava Varier (attested 2002).

Francis Vincent Tiso studied at Cornell, Harvard, and Columbia/Union Theological Seminary. Active in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies, he held visiting posts in Rome and San Francisco, and teaches Tibetan Buddhism at the Pontifical Gregorian University.

Francis Whyte Ellis was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He served in the Madras Civil Service (1796), the East India Company (~1796-1819), the Board of Revenue (1802), and as Collector at the University of Madras (1810).

Francis Wilford worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He served in the military for the East India Company (1781-1794), was a member of The Asiatic Society (~1784-1822), and served as Secretary to the committee at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1799-1822).

Francis William Bain studied at Westminster School and Oxford (Christ Church). Working in history, archaeology, and Indology, he served in the Indian Civil Service and was Professor of History and Political Economy at Deccan College from circa 1892 to 1919.

Francis Woodman Cleaves studied at Dartmouth, Harvard (Ph.D. ~1933-1942), and under Paul Pelliot (1935). Specializing in Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics, he served as a professor at Harvard University from 1941 to 1980.

Francis X. Clooney studied at Fordham and the University of Chicago (doctorate ~1978-1984). Active in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, he was Professor at Boston College (1984-2005) and Parkman Professor of Divinity and comparative theology at Harvard University from 2005.

Francis Younghusband studied at Clifton College and the Royal Military College, Sandhurst (~1881-1882). Active in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Tibetology, and religious studies, he held a post in the Foreign and Political Department in 1889.

Francisco García Ayuso studied under Martin Haug (1868) and at the University of Munich. Working in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics, he held posts at Complutense University of Madrid (1870) and Escuela Superior de Comercio de Madrid (~1886-1897).
Francisco María Rivero y Godoy earned his Ph.D. at the Complutense University of Madrid by 1866. Working in Indology, he later served there as the first Professor of Sanskrit from 1877 to 1881.

Francisco Varela studied at the University of Chile and Harvard (Ph.D. 1968-1970) under Humberto Maturana and Torsten Nils Wiesel. Working in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and neuroscience, he held posts at CNRS, Pitié-Salpêtrière Hospital, and the University of Paris.

Francisco Xavier de Santa Anna, who worked in linguistics and Indology, became a Father in the Order of Discalced Carmelites in 1790. He subsequently served as Apostolic Vicar of the Archdiocese of Verapoly from 1831 to 1844.
Francisco de Montoliú y Togores was active in Indology and religious studies. He served as a Professor at the Technical University of Madrid and founded the Theosophical Society in Spain in 1889.

id: P:Francisco de Paula Canalejas y Casas
summary: Francisco de Paula Canalejas y Casas earned his Ph.D. at Complutense University of Madrid (~1853-1858). Working in linguistics and Indology, he was Professor of Literature at the University of Valladolid (1860-1862) and eo. Professor at Complutense University of Madrid (~1860-1872).
